stem: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining search range: n, n/2, n/4, … , 1. About log₂ n halvings are needed in the worst case, so binary search is O(log n).

stem: Which of the following sorting algorithms has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
explanation: Merge sort always splits the array in half (log n levels) and merges each level in O(n), so it is O(n log n) even in the worst case. Quick sort degrades to O(n²) with bad pivots; insertion and bubble sort are O(n²) in the worst case.

stem: What is the time complexity of insertion sort when the input array of n elements is already sorted in ascending order?
explanation: For an already sorted array, each new element is compared once with its left neighbour, finds it smaller or equal, and stays in place. That is n − 1 comparisons and no shifts, so the best case is O(n).

stem:
What is the time complexity of the following pseudo-code in terms of n?

```
Integer count = 0
Integer i = 1
while (i <= n)
  for (j = 1 to i)
    count = count + 1
  end for
  i = i * 2
end while
```
explanation: i takes the values 1, 2, 4, … up to n, and the inner loop runs i times. Total work = 1 + 2 + 4 + … + 2ᵏ (2ᵏ ≤ n) = 2ᵏ⁺¹ − 1 < 2n. So the code is O(n), not O(n log n).
shortcut: Geometric series: sum is under twice the largest term

stem:
What is the final value of c when the following pseudo-code runs with n = 16?

```
Integer c = 0
for (i = 1 to n)
  Integer j = 1
  while (j < i)
    c = c + 1
    j = j * 2
  end while
end for
print c
```
explanation: For each i the inner loop runs once per power of 2 below i, i.e. ⌈log₂ i⌉ times. i = 1: 0; i = 2: 1; i = 3, 4: 2 each; i = 5–8: 3 each (12); i = 9–16: 4 each (32). Total = 0 + 1 + 4 + 12 + 32 = 49.

stem:
What is the time complexity of this pseudocode?
```
for i = 1 to n
  j = 1
  while j < n
    j = j * 2
  end while
end for
```
explanation: The outer loop runs n times. The inner loop doubles j until it reaches n, about log₂ n steps. Total work is n × log n = O(n log n).
